original_test_intent: Collect the complete Redfish Entries collection for one validated Manager LogService and verify its structural integrity without changing any entry.
original_method: Resolve the Entries link from a validated LogService, issue bounded trusted GET requests over documented pagination, validate page and entry identities/counts, redact sensitive fields and preserve the source log state.
manual_activity: Provide the target endpoint, secure credential/trust package, query size/page bounds and approved evidence retention/redaction policy; no interactive stimulus is required.
required_inputs: Validated LogService and advertised Entries link
Maximum pages, entries, bytes and elapsed time
safety_requirements: Follow only canonical same-origin pagination links
Never clear, delete, acknowledge or truncate entries
Enforce page, entry, byte and time ceilings
Detect pagination cycles and duplicate entry IDs
Store restricted raw hashes and redacted content separately
agent_execution_scope: Bind BMC, Manager, LogService and firmware identity
Capture per-page status, timing and restricted raw hash
Validate collection type/count and pagination termination
Validate unique entry IDs, canonical @odata links and parseable timestamps
Export collection summary and redacted evidence
engineer_actions: Approve evidence retention/redaction policy and collection bounds

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A GET targets the right collection class, but one curl can miss pages; the source's malformed placeholder, clear-logs step, `-k`, credentials and raw full-output behavior are unacceptable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Traverse the LogService's advertised Entries link with bounded same-origin pagination, validate every page and entry, redact sensitive content and preserve all source logs.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Manager/LogService Entries GET and 15/10 timing remain; pagination bounds, instances and entry content are supplied at runtime rather than guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use link-driven pagination with hard ceilings, consistency checks and field-aware evidence redaction.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes destructive clearing and malformed path interpolation, adds full pagination, duplicate/cycle detection, schema validation and sensitive-data governance.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers existing collection integrity only; it does not generate events or prove delivery, retention, rollover or clearing behavior.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Very large or rapidly changing logs can prevent a stable snapshot; the result must report bounded truncation or collection drift rather than claiming completeness.

project_override_considerations: If the service lacks pagination, validate a single page within the same hard response limits. Vendor entry fields may be retained only under the approved policy; do not erase fields needed for event identity from the redacted analytical view.
expected_evidence: Canonical Entries URI and collection timestamp window
Query ceilings and per-page HTTP metadata
Restricted raw hash for each page
Validated total/member counts, unique entry IDs and pagination termination
Redaction report and protected evidence location
Explicit empty, bounded-truncated or drift status

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title and GET target agree on an Entries collection. The malformed placeholder and log clearing are implementation defects, not an alternate Master intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Identity, access, bounds and redaction are identifiable inputs for deterministic read-only automation; a runtime collection failure is reported without changing the static classification.

review_improvement: Converts an unsafe one-page dump into a bounded, complete-or-explicitly-truncated, privacy-controlled log collection audit.
independent_technical_reasoning: Log collection correctness depends on more than HTTP 200. The agent must follow only server-provided same-origin pagination links, detect cycles and duplicate identities, reconcile counts and distinguish a valid empty result from missing data. Logs can contain usernames, addresses, serial numbers or tokens, so raw evidence needs restricted storage and exported evidence needs field-aware redaction. Because the workflow is entirely deterministic and read-only once normal access and policy inputs are supplied, it remains fully automatable despite the richer evidence controls.
